get.summary: List the tunnels connected to the cluster
get.description: Answers the tunnels connected to the cluster: the remote otoroshi instances that opened a tunnel to an instance of the cluster (`GET /api/tunnels/register`) and described it in the last two minutes, with the routes they expose and the instances of the cluster they are connected to. Any admin can call it.

200.description: The tunnels the remote otoroshi instances described in the last two minutes, each with its routes and the instances of the cluster it is connected to

schema.description: The tunnels connected to the cluster

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Describe how to reach this otoroshi
get.description: Answers the domain, the scheme and the exposed ports of this otoroshi: what a remote otoroshi needs to connect its tunnels to it. Any admin can call it.

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Open a tunnel from a remote otoroshi
get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket a remote otoroshi uses as a tunnel: the routes of this cluster that call the tunnel (with the `Remote tunnel calls` plugin, `otoroshi.next.tunnel.TunnelPlugin`) send their requests through it to the remote otoroshi, which routes them as if it had received them. Every message is a binary message holding a json object, its `type` telling what it is. The instance sends `request` messages (a `TunnelRequest`), and the remote otoroshi answers each with a `response` message (a `TunnelResponse` with the same `request_id`). Every 10 seconds, the remote otoroshi also sends a `ping` message, answered with a `pong` unless `pong_ping=true`, and a `tunnel_meta` message describing itself (`tunnel_id`, `name`, `routes`), listed by `GET /api/tunnels`. A `pong` message is answered with a `ping`, and with `pong_ping=true` the instance sends a `pong` message every 10 seconds. The instance lists the tunnel in its `tunnels` as a member of the cluster while it is open. Any admin can open it.

parameters.name: tunnel_id
parameters.description: The id of the tunnel (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.id` on the remote otoroshi), as listed by `GET /api/tunnels` and named by the `tunnel_id` of the `Remote tunnel calls` plugin. Several remote otoroshi instances can connect under the same id: the requests go to them in turn

parameters.name: pong_ping
parameters.description: Whether the instance sends a `pong` message every 10 seconds and answers the `pong` messages of the remote otoroshi with a `ping` (reversed keep alive), instead of answering its `ping` messages with a `pong`. False by default

101.description: The connection is upgraded to a websocket

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), or the `tunnel_id` query parameter is missing

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

404.description: The tunnels are disabled on this instance (`otoroshi.tunnels.enabled`)

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Open a relay to a tunnel
get.description: Upgrades the connection to a websocket another instance of the cluster uses to send requests to a tunnel connected to this instance (when `otoroshi.tunnels.worker-ws` is enabled, the default). Every message is a binary message holding a json object: the other instance sends `request` messages (a `TunnelRequest`) and `ping` messages; this instance answers `response` messages (a `TunnelResponse`, with the `request_id` of the request, a 404 answer when the tunnel is not connected here) and `pong` messages. Any admin can open it.

parameters.name: tunnelId
parameters.description: The id of a tunnel connected to this instance (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.id` on the remote otoroshi), as listed by `GET /api/tunnels`

parameters.name: mid
parameters.description: The id of the instance the relay is meant for (the `id` of the member): the connection is refused with a 417 when it is not this one. Sent when the instances reach each other through a load balancer (`otoroshi.tunnels.worker-use-loadbalancing`), the caller retrying until it reaches the right one

101.description: The connection is upgraded to a websocket

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

404.description: The tunnels are disabled on this instance (`otoroshi.tunnels.enabled`)

417.description: The `mid` query parameter is not the id of this instance

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

post.summary: Send a request to a tunnel
post.description: Sends the request of the body through a tunnel connected to this instance, and answers the answer of the remote otoroshi, wrapped in a `TunnelResponse`. When the tunnel is not connected to this instance, the wrapped answer is a 404 (`missing local tunnel`), the call itself answering 200. Any admin can call it.

parameters.name: tunnelId
parameters.description: The id of a tunnel connected to this instance (`otoroshi.tunnels.<key>.id` on the remote otoroshi), as listed by `GET /api/tunnels`

requestBody.description: The request to send through the tunnel, as the instances of the cluster write it

200.description: The answer of the remote otoroshi wrapped in a `TunnelResponse`, whatever its status: a 404 one when the tunnel is not connected to this instance

400.description: The credentials are missing, or the body is not json

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or the global configuration makes the admin api read only (`apiReadOnly`) and the call is not a GET

404.description: The tunnels are disabled on this instance (`otoroshi.tunnels.enabled`)

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded
